Cell aggregate confirms agent, mode, task identity, artifact status, protocol status, subagent count, timing, and aggregate quality fields for this run.
Current status contains the authoritative completed official evaluation record and protocol validation details used to resolve the outcome.
Evaluator summary reports the RepoZero C2Rust official Docker evaluator result, testcase counts, pass rate, and process status.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server transport journal records session lifecycle, prompt completion, and transport events; semantic action evidence is projected into actor wire ledgers.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the workspace session directory and confirms the working directory used by the run.
Explorer child agent-0 probed pluralize and singularize behavior with many black-box executable runs and returned a detailed behavioral spec without modifying files.
Explorer child agent-1 probed camelize, underscore, classify, and tableize behavior and returned exact outputs and implementation rules without writes.
Explorer child agent-2 probed humanize, titleize, dasherize, and parameterize behavior, including punctuation and whitespace, and returned a detailed read-only spec.
Explorer child agent-3 probed upcase, downcase, capitalize, CLI edge behavior, and output formatting, including empty and multi-argument cases.
Coder child agent-4 created the Cargo project and root test13.rs, iteratively fixed mismatches found by differential tests, and ended with clean build and fuzz results.
Parallel parent entered swarm mode, delegated four focused probes and one implementation task, inspected files, reran independent checks, and finalized the passing solution.

timeline_reviews.summary: Serial server transport journal records one non-delegated session lifecycle, tool calls, completion, and final response.
Session index maps the serial session id to its workspace session directory and confirms the working directory used by the run.
Serial main actor probed the executable, wrote a complete Cargo project and root test13.rs, fixed a rustc edition command issue, and verified with differential and fuzz tests.

parallel.requirements: The run treated the task as a std-only Rust 2021 black-box reimplementation of test13 with exact CLI and output behavior and required /output/test13.rs plus Cargo project files.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed the executable, launched four read-only explorer children by API group, then delegated implementation to coder child agent-4 and kept parent-level verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Agent-4 wrote a Cargo project with src/lib.rs, src/pluralize.rs, src/text.rs, and root test13.rs, then iteratively fixed singularization edge cases found by differential and fuzz checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Implementation was written into the required /output tree, inspected by the parent, and left as a Cargo project with a release binary artifact and root entry file.
parallel.verification: Agent-4 ran cargo and rustc builds, differential checks, and fuzzing; the parent then independently reran a shell differential check after a python3 attempt failed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work remained at closure; official evaluation completed and passed all 39 evaluated test cases.

serial.requirements: The run treated the task as a std-only Rust 2021 black-box migration with exact CLI/output matching, no external crates, and required /output project artifacts.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, rule inference, implementation, build repair, verification, and final response without any subagent or delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote Cargo.toml, test13.rs, and an inflection module tree under inflection/ with byte-oriented casing and number helpers.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was assembled directly in /output, built with Cargo, then compiled with rustc --edition 2021 after a default-edition failure.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran 39 hand-picked differential cases including no-arg and edge inputs, then fuzzed 300 random inputs; official evaluation also passed 39/39.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work remained at closure; the earlier rustc command error was corrected before final response and official evaluation passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the required Rust 2021, std-only, black-box reimplementation with a root test13.rs and byte-for-byte CLI output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same prompt requirements and implemented the same thirteen output calls for one optional argv word.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference; both accepted the black-box executable as oracle and delivered a Cargo/rustc-capable Rust project.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent split behavior discovery into four explorer children and assigned implementation to a coder child, then retained parent verification ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: One actor handled probing, writing, build fixes, differential testing, fuzzing, and final reporting without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used explicit subtask ownership and a separate coder owner; serial kept all ownership local. Both ownership models reached a complete deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs were scoped by API groups and returned behavioral specs; the coder child received the aggregated implementation task and reported files/tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor accumulated its own probe findings directly and immediately used them in the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had handoff boundaries but the returned specs were usable and later consumed; serial avoided those boundaries by staying in one context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Coder child produced a modular project under src/lib.rs, src/pluralize.rs, src/text.rs, and test13.rs, refining singularization after mismatch and fuzz evidence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a different module layout under inflection/mod.rs, inflection/casing.rs, inflection/number.rs, plus test13.rs, using simpler inferred rules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete code organization and rule breadth differed, but both generated accepted artifacts and byte-for-byte matching behavior for evaluator cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Explorer and coder child results returned to the parent; the parent inspected files and reran final checks before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child result lifecycle existed; all intermediate findings remained in the serial actor context until final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra result-return and adoption steps, but none were lost, trapped, or ignored; serial had a simpler lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the coder child wrote the project files; the parent read them and ran builds/tests, with no competing implementation writes among live children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote its own project files directly and compiled in the same workspace without cross-agent shared-state coordination.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared output workspace but avoided write collisions because explorer children were read-only and the coder owned implementation writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Coder child ran cargo, rustc, fixed differential mismatches, fuzzed, and parent reran an independent shell differential check before official 39/39 pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo, retried rustc with edition 2021, compared 39 cases, fuzzed 300 inputs, and official evaluation passed 39/39.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel performed broader child-level fuzzing plus parent recheck; serial performed a narrower but sufficient independent verification path. Official acceptance matched.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent substantially more time and tokens with five subagents, but completed before timeout and left no unfinished required work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed much faster with no subagents and no timeout, also leaving no unfinished required work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was costlier and slower, but the extra budget did not cause a closure failure; both final statuses were finished and passed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current cell/status.json evaluations completed and passed 39 of 39 test cases. The parallel run achieved success through multi-agent black-box probing plus a coder child and parent recheck, while the serial run achieved success through a single-actor probe, implementation, build repair, and verification path.
parallel_contributors: Parallel decomposition increased behavioral probing breadth and produced a detailed child implementation that passed its own tests and the parent recheck.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided coordination boundaries and still produced a complete accepted implementation through direct probing and local verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used src/lib.rs, src/pluralize.rs, and src/text.rs with broader singularization rules; serial used inflection/mod.rs, casing.rs, and number.rs with simpler rules sufficient for official tests.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; strategy differences are descriptive rather than causal for pass versus fail

Rejected because final assembly and placement were owned by the coder child, which wrote Cargo.toml, src files, and root test13.rs before verification.
Rejected because the parent managed the end-to-end sequence from probing through child implementation, inspection, independent verification, and final delivery.
Rejected because the exploratory probes were useful parallel evidence gathering, not a mandatory serial gate that blocked all productive work into an incomplete closure window.
Rejected because although implementation followed the explorer reports, the investigative phase returned usable findings and did not leave implementation or verification incomplete.
Rejected because the indispensable implementation path had an assigned coder child and completed with final project files and verification.
Rejected because four explorer children and one coder child did not exhaust the run budget; the run completed normally and passed official evaluation.
Rejected because the broad coder assignment completed, corrected mismatches, built artifacts, and returned a usable summary; no indispensable work was left unfinished.
Rejected because child briefs stated their scoped API groups, black-box constraint, no-source/no-write limits for explorers, and the coder brief included delivery and verification obligations.
Rejected because independently implemented components were not delegated to multiple agents; explorer outputs were specs and the single coder child owned the implementation.
Rejected because returned findings were not shown to disappear in transfer; the coder and parent acted on the behavioral specs and verified the resulting project.
Rejected because the handoffs were lengthy but consumed successfully; no dependent implementation or decision was left unfinished due to report volume.
Rejected because no child result described a superseded workspace or requirement state that was later consumed to cause rework or invalid verification.
Rejected because no incompatible child reports remained unadjudicated at a decision point; mismatches were ordinary implementation refinements fixed before final verification.
Rejected because the parent did not merely accept file existence or child success; it inspected generated files and reran an independent integrated differential check before completion.
Rejected because there was no replacement child repeating prior work without inherited state; failed python checks were handled locally by switching to shell checks.

Rejected because completed artifacts were promoted and verified before closure; there was no directly promotable candidate left unplaced at shutdown.
Rejected because final implementation edits preceded the final build, differential checks, fuzz checks, and parent independent verification.
Rejected because the coder child wrote the implementation into /output and the parent read those files and used them for the final acceptance checks.
Rejected because no verifier child produced a trapped finding; verification evidence was visible to the coder and then independently rerun by the parent.
Rejected because observed command failures and mismatches were taken over and fixed by the responsible actor before final closure.
Rejected because the parent consumed the AgentSwarm result to commission implementation and later inspected the generated project before finalizing.
Rejected because the parent did not wait blindly to timeout; it received child results, inspected artifacts, and ran an independent differential check.
Rejected because explorer children were read-only and the coder child alone owned implementation files; no competing designs required reconciliation.
Rejected because no two live agents edited the same source or configuration file with a visible reconciliation conflict.
Rejected because there is no proven replacement of non-entry source actively owned by another agent; implementation files were written by the coder owner.
Rejected because no live actor replaced a required entry point or executable while another actor owned or used it; builds happened after the coder wrote the deliverable.
Rejected because no broad cleanup or rebuild invalidated another agent final-tree contribution or provenance.
Rejected because the shared workspace did not cause unstable state or provenance loss; only the coder child performed implementation writes.
Rejected because no generated artifact, cache, fixture, or temporary script from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as the stable reference environment.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no candidate cleared the retained-pattern gate because no adverse parallel coordination consequence materialized.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Potential near matches around serial investigation, large handoffs, shared workspace, and failed local commands were rejected because they did not cause lost work, omitted integration, unverified closure, or failure.
